blocks.text: This closing topic of the module goes beyond the citation mechanics already covered in the Citation Prompting topic, treating source attribution as a broader design concern, how it builds user trust, what granularity it should operate at, and how it ties together with everything else covered in this module into one complete RAG prompt.

This topic covers why attribution matters for trust, choosing between document-level and sentence-level granularity, attributing claims correctly within a synthesized answer, and closes by combining every technique from this module into one complete, worked RAG prompt example.
1. Source Attribution as More Than Citation Formatting

blocks.alt: Building on answer synthesis prompting, source attribution closes out this module

blocks.text: The earlier Citation Prompting topic covered the mechanics of getting a model to produce citations, explicit instructions, format consistency, verification, source attribution here is the broader design question, what attribution is actually for, at what level of detail, and how it fits into everything else this module has covered.
2. Citation Mechanics vs the Broader Attribution Concern

blocks.alt: Citation prompting covers the mechanics, source attribution covers the broader design concern

blocks.text: Where citation prompting answers how do you get a model to produce a citation, source attribution answers a different question, what should actually be attributed, at what granularity, and why does it matter to the person actually reading the answer.
3. Why Attribution Builds User Trust

blocks.alt: No visible sourcing produces lower user trust, clear attribution produces higher user trust

blocks.text: A response with no visible connection to its underlying sources asks a reader to simply trust it, a response that clearly shows where each claim came from lets a reader verify it directly, this transparency is often what actually earns trust in an AI system output, especially for anything the reader considers genuinely important.
4. Document-Level vs Sentence-Level Attribution

blocks.alt: Document level attribution identifies which document, sentence level identifies which exact passage

blocks.text: Attribution can operate at different levels of granularity, document-level attribution says which source document a claim came from, sentence-level attribution points to the exact supporting passage, this connects directly to the direct quote requirement covered in the earlier Grounding Techniques topic, sentence-level attribution is grounding made visible to the reader.

blocks.text: 5. Attribution Within a Synthesized Answer

blocks.alt: A synthesized, multi source answer gets each claim attributed to its source

blocks.text: This connects directly back to the previous topic, answer synthesis prompting, a genuinely well synthesized answer combines information fluently while still allowing each individual claim within it to be traced back to its specific supporting source, attribution is what makes that traceability visible and usable to an actual reader.
6. Attribution as a Compliance Consideration

blocks.alt: A regulated or high stakes domain turns attribution into a real requirement

blocks.text: In certain domains, legal research, medical information, financial guidance, clear source attribution is not merely a nice user experience touch, it can be a genuine requirement, allowing a professional reader to verify a claim against its original source before relying on it in a consequential decision.

blocks.title: This connects to the output constraints concept from an earlier module
blocks.content: A mandatory attribution requirement for certain response types functions exactly like the system-level output constraints covered in an earlier module, something that must always appear, not left to the model discretion.

blocks.text: 7. Bringing Every Technique in This Module Together

blocks.alt: Retrieval, grounding, hallucination reduction, multi document handling, synthesis, and attribution combine into one complete prompt

blocks.text: A genuinely well constructed RAG prompt combines everything covered across this module, retrieval prompting fundamentals, grounding techniques, hallucination reduction instructions, multi-document handling, answer synthesis guidance, and attribution requirements, all working together in one coherent prompt design.

code.content:
prompt = f"""
Answer the question using only the documents below. Quote exact supporting
text for each claim. If documents conflict, note the conflict. Synthesize
information across documents into one coherent answer organized by theme,
not by source. Cite which document supports each claim. If the documents
do not contain enough information, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

Document A:
{doc_a}

Document B:
{doc_b}

Question:
{question}
"""

blocks.text: 8. Testing the Complete Pipeline End to End

This connects to the system prompt evaluation checklist covered in an earlier module, a complete RAG prompt combining every technique from this module deserves the same thorough, whole-pipeline testing, not just testing each technique individually, but confirming they all work correctly together against realistic, varied questions and document sets.
9. This Module Is Now Complete

This closes out the RAG Prompting module, retrieval prompting, grounding techniques, hallucination reduction, multi-document prompting, answer synthesis, and now source attribution, together forming a complete toolkit for constructing reliable, trustworthy retrieval augmented prompts, the next module, Agent Prompting, covers prompting techniques for systems that take real actions, building on the ReAct technique introduced in an earlier module.
Worked Example

A team builds a legal research assistant that synthesizes answers from multiple retrieved case documents, an early version produces fluent, well organized answers but with only vague document-level attribution, a compliance reviewer flags that legal professionals need to verify claims against exact passages, not just a general document reference.

Upgrading to sentence-level attribution, requiring the model to quote the exact supporting passage for each claim alongside the document reference, satisfies the actual compliance requirement while preserving the readable, synthesized answer structure the team had already built, demonstrating how attribution granularity needs to match the actual stakes of the domain.
Common Mistakes

items: Treating attribution purely as a citation formatting detail rather than a genuine trust and verification concern
Using document-level attribution alone in a domain where sentence-level verification genuinely matters
Losing individual claim attribution once information gets synthesized into a combined, fluent answer
Testing each RAG prompting technique from this module individually but never testing the complete combined pipeline together

blocks.text: Practice

Take the complete RAG prompt example from this topic, adapt it to a domain you are familiar with, and test it end to end with a multi-document scenario including at least one conflicting detail, checking that grounding, synthesis, and attribution all work correctly together.
Key Takeaway

Source attribution is a broader design concern beyond citation mechanics, about what level of detail actually builds reader trust and enables verification, and a genuinely well constructed RAG prompt brings together retrieval, grounding, hallucination reduction, multi-document handling, synthesis, and attribution as one coherent, thoroughly tested whole rather than a collection of separately applied techniques.
